title: Choosing a location

2026-11-01T08:14:02Z confirm: Claude Opus 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

changes: Add a note that some businesses, such as online-only sellers, need no physical site, so location may not be a choice for them.
Check that the location factors match the VCE Business Management Units 1 and 2 study design wording, including access.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same idea of weighing customers, suppliers, staff, competitors and costs at the right Year 11 depth, but it does not cover the brief's point that some businesses need no physical site.

confirm.reason: The bank card covers customers, suppliers, staff, rent and competitors. This brief also needs access and whether the business needs a physical site at all, such as operating online, and adding those would be new content rather than a small change.

draft.title: Choosing a location
card: A business chooses where to set up. Location is part of the internal environment, because the owner decides it.
Factors to weigh include customers nearby, rent and other costs, competitors, suppliers, staff and access, such as parking, public transport and roads.
The best site depends on the business. A café needs foot traffic. A bakery that supplies other shops may want cheap rent and easy deliveries.
Some businesses do not need a physical site. A freelance web designer can work from home and serve clients anywhere, so the factors above matter less.
draft.remember: Match the site to what the business needs most, or ask if it needs a site at all.

a.q: Which choice shows a business weighing access when choosing a location?
opts: Choosing a site with parking and a train stop nearby
Choosing a site with the lowest rent in the suburb
Choosing a site next to a rival that sells the same goods
Choosing a site close to where the owner lives
a.why: Access is about how easily customers, staff and deliveries can reach the site, so parking and a train stop are access. Low rent is a cost factor, not access.
a.clue: Think about how people and deliveries reach the site.

b.q: Priya runs an online tutoring service from her home in Bendigo. Her students are across Victoria and lessons are by video. Why is location a minor factor for her?
opts: She does not need a physical site to reach customers
She has no costs, so rent does not matter to her
She has no competitors in her local area
She can only work in the suburb where she lives
b.why: Priya delivers lessons by video, so her customers do not need to visit a site. This makes foot traffic, parking and nearby customers matter less. She still has costs, such as internet and equipment, so having no costs is wrong.
b.clue: Do her customers ever need to come to her?

a.best: Choosing a site with parking and a train stop nearby

b.best: She does not need a physical site to reach customers

check.summary: No problems found. The card treats location as an internal, owner-chosen factor, consistent with the chapter, and both questions have one clearly defensible answer.
